fact: Kenya's Civil Registration Services says its CRVS system is integrated with the National ID system, so parents' National ID details are held in birth registration records and parents' details are verified during birth registration.

Kenya's Health Cabinet Secretary said a biometric campaign under the Social Health Authority system is enrolling children aged 7 to 17 into Maisha Namba, to link each child's health record to the digital ID; no date is given for the start, so the publication date is used.

Kenya's Registration of Telecommunications Service Subscribers Regulations 2025 (Legal Notice No. 90), reported by the State Department for Immigration and Citizen Services, require biometric and ID verification for SIM registration and recognise the Refugee Identity Card as valid for it, with a six-month compliance window for existing subscribers.

fact: The Kenyan State Department for Immigration and Citizen Services says the electronic ID card introduced on 1 November 2023 can be validated through KYC to support SIM card registration and opening bank accounts.
The same presentation gives SIM card registration (telecoms) and bank account opening (banking) as transactions the Maisha Card is validated for through KYC.

The presentation says the Maisha Integrated Database has an eKYC layer through which relying agencies request validation, answered only with Boolean yes/no values, and that data goes only to whitelisted relying agencies.

Smile ID (Smile Identity) verifies identities against government databases in real time for fintechs and enterprises across 30+ African countries, naming Kenya among its markets (2023 funding announcement, no month given; published date used).
